idiom_name: consumer-side interface + struct owning *http.Client (or a generated gRPC client)
implementation_notes: The delegate is a small struct that owns the transport (*http.Client, a gRPC connection, or another pooled client) and satisfies a narrow interface declared next to the consumer; error translation wraps causes with fmt.Errorf("%w", ...) and can expose sentinel errors checked by errors.Is/errors.As. The lookup role collapses into construction-time configuration or a sync.Once-guarded lazy dial. The classic delegate/lookup/service split is unnecessary—one struct plus the consumer-side interface is the whole pattern—but a hand-written wrapper still earns its place over a generated client when it caches bounded lookups, aggregates calls, maps status and transport failures, or owns retry policy.
pitfalls: http.Client is safe for concurrent use, but the zero value has no timeout - set Timeout or rely on context deadlines, or one hung service blocks every handler.
Wrapping with %w preserves the cause for errors.Is/errors.As; converting to a bare sentinel throws the diagnostic away.
Never store request-scoped state (auth token, deadline) in the struct - keep the delegate stateless and pass context.Context per call.
